picks.editorial_note: OpenAI reportedly solved the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of the seven Clay Millennium Prize problems — if it holds up, it's one of the most significant AI-for-mathematics results to date, discussed here by a Stony Brook mathematician.
picks.title: Solving for Tomorrow: James Glimm on Mathematics, AI and Life

picks.editorial_note: The UK's AI Minister marked a construction milestone on the nation's most powerful supercomputer, a flagship government-university partnership meant to power drug discovery and climate research at national scale.
picks.title: AI Minister marks milestone on Supercomputer build | News | The University of Edinburgh

picks.editorial_note: France's €13.5M government-backed AI Evaluation Program at Inria establishes a national scientific roadmap for AI safety and robustness testing, a direct policy response to growing concern over AI risk.
picks.title: France 2030 | Launch of the AI Evaluation Program: a scientific roadmap for the evaluation and safety of artificial intelligence

picks.editorial_note: SRI's $26.5M ARPA-H award to build an AI 'co-pilot' for rural medical care shows federal funding translating directly into deployable technology addressing real healthcare access gaps.
picks.title: Reuters covers SRI's work in the ARPA-H-funded PARADIGM program - SRI

picks.editorial_note: An international team including Science Tokyo built a protein language model unifying sequence and 3D structure data, a scientifically significant advance for mapping evolutionary and functional relationships across the protein universe.
picks.title: Uniting sequence and structure to map the protein universe | Science Tokyo

picks.editorial_note: UCLA's 'physical AI' work — using self-organized nanowire networks as hardware-based neural networks — points toward a fundamentally different, more energy-efficient computing paradigm for AI.
picks.title: Toward physical AI: When the hardware becomes the neural network

picks.editorial_note: NSF's new ELEGANT program funds translation of low-dimensional semiconductor research into U.S. manufacturing, a strategic bet on maintaining domestic leadership in the microelectronics that underpin AI hardware.
picks.title: NSF invests in translating low-dimensional semiconductor technologies to establish U.S. leadership in microelectronics

picks.editorial_note: Edinburgh's Genome Foundry secured a three-year ARIA-backed partnership to expand AI- and robotics-driven biofoundry work, linking a UK government innovation agency directly to academic biological research infrastructure.
picks.title: Funding boost transforms AI-enabled biological research | News | The University of Edinburgh

picks.editorial_note: EPFL and ETH Zurich's open-source Apertus model is being integrated into Proton's privacy-focused Lumo assistant, instantly exposing academic AI research to tens of millions of real-world users.
picks.title: Apertus partners with Proton's Lumo AI assistant

picks.editorial_note: A DOE Genesis Mission-funded project at UNR uses AI to reason over decades of nuclear waste safety-case evidence, an application with direct implications for regulatory decisions on nuclear safety.
picks.title: AI project reviews nuclear waste safety-case evidence
